definition: A very large model trained on broad data at scale that can be adapted to many downstream tasks and domains.
details: The Stanford “foundation models” report coined the term to describe models trained on broad data with massive scale, whose emergent capabilities are then steered by fine-tuning, prompting or adapters. They function as a shared substrate that many applications build upon, raising both opportunities (few-shot learning, transfer) and risks (bias, misuse, environmental cost).

citation.title: On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models
